findings.title: Spawned workers fail the multiprocessing.Process type check
findings.body: Workers are created using multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently, this isinstance check is false for production workers, so an unhealthy worker is never killed before its replacement starts. A hung worker that later resumes can flush the same shards concurrently with its replacement. The identical check in join() also prevents terminating workers that exceed the shutdown timeout. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from spawned processes in both places.

findings.title: Shutdown skips remaining workers when the shared deadline expires
findings.body: When the join deadline expires, this break skips every remaining worker without attempting to terminate it. With multiple flusher processes, one worker blocked on Redis or Kafka can consume the entire timeout, leaving other blocked workers alive after join() returns. During rebalancing, those workers can outlive their partition assignment and overlap with new flushers. Stop waiting once the deadline expires, but still perform termination cleanup for every worker.
